issues.description: New command names break the singular `:quickmark-*` / `:bookmark-*` naming convention used by every sibling command
issues.detail: The new commands are `quickmarks_reload` / `bookmarks_reload` (exposed as `:quickmarks-reload` / `:bookmarks-reload`), while all existing siblings use singular form: `quickmark-save`, `quickmark-add`, `bookmark-add`, `bookmark-load`. This breaks an implicit naming contract users and callers rely on. Rename to `quickmark-reload` / `bookmark-reload`.

issues.description: reload() clears marks before parsing, leaving partial state if parsing raises
issues.detail: `reload()` calls `marks.clear()` then re-reads the file. If `_init_lineparser` or `_parse_line` raises (malformed line, I/O error, InvalidUrlError), `marks` is left empty while the on-disk file is intact and `changed` may not be emitted consistently. Build the new dict first, swap atomically, then emit once — postcondition should be 'matches disk OR unchanged'.

issues.description: changed signal now fires from __init__ via reload(), altering the construction-time contract
issues.detail: Previously `__init__` populated `marks` without emitting `changed`; routing init through `reload()` causes `changed.emit()` to fire during construction, before `_init_savemanager` runs. Subscribers assuming `changed` means a post-init mutation will see a spurious initial event, and the autosave pathway may be perturbed. Suppress the signal during construction or document the new behavior.

issues.description: Unit test does not cover removal semantics or the QuickmarkManager path
issues.detail: `test_reload` only verifies one entry being replaced by another in `BookmarkManager`. It does not assert that entries removed from disk disappear from `marks`, nor does it exercise `QuickmarkManager.reload()`, which overrides `_parse_line` and reads a different file. Add cases with disjoint before/after sets and cover the quickmark path.

issues.description: New Gherkin scenarios are unnamed and only assert the user-visible message
issues.detail: Both new `Scenario:` blocks lack titles, breaking the file's naming pattern and hurting traceability. They also only check that the info message appears — they do not mutate the file on disk between writes and assert that in-memory marks reflect the new contents. Name the scenarios and assert the actual reload effect.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a SALVAGEABLE verdict: the refactor's shape (lift load logic into a `reload()` method owned by `UrlMarkManager`) is sound, but four issues need addressing before merge. The new command names break the singular `:quickmark-*` / `:bookmark-*` convention; `reload()` clears state before parsing, so a parse error leaves the manager half-populated; and routing `__init__` through `reload()` silently changes the construction-time contract by emitting `changed` during init. Test coverage is thin — the unit test only covers replacement (not removal or the QuickmarkManager path), and the BDD scenarios are unnamed and only assert the info message. Fix: align names, parse-then-swap, suppress or document the init-time signal, and tighten tests.
